property_tests.description: For any integer value supplied for check_interval, rebuild_poll_interval, or max_resolve_retries, the stored value equals max(min_bound, min(v, max_bound)) as declared by Clamped.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample integers uniformly from [-1000, 1000] for each of check_interval (bounds: ge=60), rebuild_poll_interval (bounds: ge=2), rebuild_timeout (bounds: ge=1), and max_resolve_retries (bounds: ge=0, le=10) using hypothesis.strategies.integers(min_value=-1000, max_value=1000)
property_tests.invariant_check: cp = CarryPatchConfig(check_interval=v1, rebuild_poll_interval=v2, rebuild_timeout=v3, max_resolve_retries=v4); assert cp.check_interval == max(60, v1); assert cp.rebuild_poll_interval == max(2, v2); assert cp.rebuild_timeout == max(1, v3); assert cp.max_resolve_retries == max(0, min(v4, 10))

property_tests.description: For any combination of CLI flags, environment variables, and config values, carry-patch mode is active if and only if both the resolved workspace slug and resolved PAT are non-empty strings.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample from hypothesis.strategies.text() for workspace_flag, AF_WORKSPACE, config_workspace, token_flag, AF_HUB_TOKEN; include empty string in the sample space; use hypothesis.strategies.one_of(st.just(''), st.text(min_size=1)) for each source
property_tests.invariant_check: resolved_slug = workspace_flag or os.environ.get('AF_WORKSPACE', '') or config_workspace; resolved_pat = token_flag or os.environ.get('AF_HUB_TOKEN', ''); carry_patch_active = bool(resolved_slug) and bool(resolved_pat); assert carry_patch_mode_activated(result) == carry_patch_active

property_tests.description: For any combination of --hub-url flag, AF_HUB_URL env var, and config.hub.endpoint_url, the resolved hub URL is the first non-empty value in the priority order: CLI flag > AF_HUB_URL > config.hub.endpoint_url.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample from hypothesis.strategies.one_of(st.just(''), st.from_regex(r'https://[a-z]+\.example\.com', fullmatch=True)) for each of hub_url_flag, af_hub_url_env, and config_endpoint_url independently
property_tests.invariant_check: expected = hub_url_flag or af_hub_url_env or config_endpoint_url; resolved = resolve_hub_url(hub_url_flag=hub_url_flag, config_url=config_endpoint_url) with AF_HUB_URL=af_hub_url_env in env; assert resolved == expected

property_tests.description: For any startup invocation with carry-patch mode active, the daemon loop starts if and only if all six CWD validation steps pass; any single step failure causes process exit with code 1.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Enumerate all failure modes: HubAuthError, HubForbiddenError, HubNotFoundError, wrong workspace_mode, non-ready clone_status ('pending'/'cloning'/'failed'), FileNotFoundError from git, TimeoutExpired from git, non-zero git return code, URL mismatch; for each, mock exactly that failure while all others succeed
property_tests.invariant_check: for each failure_mode in all_failure_modes: with inject_failure(failure_mode): result = invoke_full_startup(); assert result.exit_code == 1; assert daemon_runner_not_called(); with all_passing(): result = invoke_full_startup(); assert result.exit_code == 0; assert daemon_runner_called()

property_tests.description: For any startup invocation where .nightshift/config.toml already exists, the content of the file is identical before and after nightshift startup.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample arbitrary file content strings using hypothesis.strategies.text(min_size=1, max_size=10000) as the pre-existing config.toml content; run config generation with various resolved values
property_tests.invariant_check: with tmp_cwd() as cwd: config_path = cwd / '.nightshift' / 'config.toml'; config_path.parent.mkdir(); config_path.write_text(original_content); run_config_generation(...); assert config_path.read_text() == original_content

property_tests.description: For any startup invocation that generates .nightshift/config.toml, the generated file contains no PAT or token value.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample arbitrary PAT strings using hypothesis.strategies.text(min_size=1, max_size=200, alphabet=hypothesis.strategies.characters(whitelist_categories=('Lu','Ll','Nd'))) to represent realistic token values
property_tests.invariant_check: with tmp_cwd() as cwd: run_config_generation(pat=arbitrary_pat); content = (cwd / '.nightshift' / 'config.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8'); assert arbitrary_pat not in content

property_tests.description: For any exception raised by set_variable during startup, nightshift emits a warning log and proceeds to start the daemon loop; it never exits due to a set_variable failure.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample from the set of all HubError subclasses: [HubAuthError, HubNotFoundError, HubForbiddenError, HubConnectionError, HubConflictError, generic HubError]; also include generic Exception; inject each as the exception raised by set_variable
property_tests.invariant_check: for exc_class in all_hub_error_classes + [Exception]: with mock_hub_client(set_variable_raises=exc_class()), mock_daemon_runner() as mock_runner: invoke_full_startup(); assert mock_runner.run.called; assert not process_exited_with_error()

property_tests.description: For any startup invocation with carry-patch mode active, exactly one HubClient instance is constructed and reused for get_workspace and both set_variable calls.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample valid startup configurations (non-empty hub_url, slug, pat) using hypothesis.strategies.fixed_dictionaries with text fields; vary which set_variable calls succeed or fail
property_tests.invariant_check: with track_hub_client_instantiation() as tracker: asyncio.run(startup_helper(hub_url=hub_url, pat=pat, slug=slug, ...)); assert tracker.instantiation_count == 1; assert tracker.instance.get_workspace.called; assert tracker.instance.set_variable.call_count == 2

edge_case_tests.expected: config.carry_patch.max_resolve_retries == 0; no ValidationError is raised
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: cp = CarryPatchConfig(max_resolve_retries=0); assert cp.max_resolve_retries == 0

preconditions: packages/afcore/afcore/core/config.py contains CarryPatchConfig with Clamped(ge=60) on check_interval
edge_case_tests.input: CarryPatchConfig(check_interval=60)
edge_case_tests.expected: config.carry_patch.check_interval == 60; no ValidationError is raised

edge_case_tests.description: An existing config file without [hub] or [carry_patch] sections loads successfully with defaults, confirming backward compatibility.
preconditions: packages/afcore/afcore/core/config.py has AgentFoxConfig with hub and carry_patch fields using default_factory
edge_case_tests.input: TOML string representing a pre-existing config file with only legacy sections (e.g. [nightshift]) and no [hub] or [carry_patch]
edge_case_tests.expected: AgentFoxConfig loads without error; config.carry_patch.enabled == False; config.hub.endpoint_url == ''
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: toml_str = '[nightshift]\nsome_key = "value"'; config = parse_afcore_config(toml_str); assert config.carry_patch.enabled == False; assert config.hub.endpoint_url == ''

edge_case_tests.description: nightshift CLI uses the --token flag value as the PAT directly without calling resolve_hub_pat() when --token is supplied.
preconditions: AF_HUB_TOKEN is unset in the environment
resolve_hub_pat is mocked to track calls
edge_case_tests.input: CLI invocation: nightshift --workspace my-slug --hub-url https://hub.example.com --token cli-token-value
edge_case_tests.expected: resolved PAT == 'cli-token-value'; resolve_hub_pat() is not called
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: with mock_resolve_hub_pat() as mock_pat, mock_hub_client() as mock_client: invoke_cli(['--workspace', 'my-slug', '--hub-url', 'https://hub.example.com', '--token', 'cli-token-value']); assert mock_client.constructor_args.pat == 'cli-token-value'; assert mock_pat.call_count == 0

edge_case_tests.description: nightshift CLI prefers the --hub-url flag value over AF_HUB_URL environment variable when both are set.
preconditions: AF_HUB_URL is set to 'https://env.hub.example.com' in the environment
resolve_hub_url returns the flag value when hub_url_flag is non-empty
edge_case_tests.input: CLI invocation: nightshift --hub-url https://flag.hub.example.com --workspace my-slug --token myPAT with AF_HUB_URL=https://env.hub.example.com
edge_case_tests.expected: resolved hub URL == 'https://flag.hub.example.com'
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: with env({'AF_HUB_URL': 'https://env.hub.example.com'}), mock_hub_client() as mock_client: invoke_cli(['--hub-url', 'https://flag.hub.example.com', '--workspace', 'my-slug', '--token', 'myPAT']); assert mock_client.constructor_args.endpoint_url == 'https://flag.hub.example.com'

edge_case_tests.description: nightshift CLI exits with code 1 when all three hub URL resolution tiers are empty strings and carry-patch mode is otherwise active.
edge_case_tests.input: CLI invocation: nightshift --workspace my-slug --token myPAT with no hub URL source
edge_case_tests.expected: process exits with code 1; stderr contains a message about hub URL being required
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: result = invoke_cli(['--workspace', 'my-slug', '--token', 'myPAT']); assert result.exit_code == 1; assert 'hub' in result.stderr.lower()

edge_case_tests.description: The async startup helper strips trailing whitespace from the local origin URL before comparing to workspace.git_url, avoiding false mismatches.
edge_case_tests.input: async startup helper invoked; git stdout has trailing newline
edge_case_tests.expected: CWD validation passes; no URL mismatch error is raised; logging.info is called
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: workspace = Workspace(workspace_mode='carry_patch', clone_status='ready', git_url='https://git.example.com/repo.git'); with mock_hub_client(get_workspace_returns=workspace), mock_subprocess_run(returncode=0, stdout=b'https://git.example.com/repo.git\n'), capture_logs() as logs: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); assert any('valid' in m.lower() or 'success' in m.lower() for m in [r.message for r in logs if r.levelname == 'INFO'])

edge_case_tests.description: The async startup helper exits with code 1 and shows 'pending' in the error message when clone_status is 'pending'.
edge_case_tests.input: async startup helper invoked; workspace.clone_status == 'pending'
edge_case_tests.expected: process exits with code 1; stderr contains 'pending'
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: workspace = Workspace(workspace_mode='carry_patch', clone_status='pending', git_url='https://git.example.com/repo.git'); with mock_hub_client(get_workspace_returns=workspace): with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); assert exc_info.value.code == 1; assert 'pending' in captured_stderr

edge_case_tests.description: The async startup helper exits with code 1 and shows 'failed' in the error message when clone_status is 'failed'.
edge_case_tests.input: async startup helper invoked; workspace.clone_status == 'failed'
edge_case_tests.expected: process exits with code 1; stderr contains 'failed'
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: workspace = Workspace(workspace_mode='carry_patch', clone_status='failed', git_url='https://git.example.com/repo.git'); with mock_hub_client(get_workspace_returns=workspace): with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); assert exc_info.value.code == 1; assert 'failed' in captured_stderr

edge_case_tests.description: The async startup helper exits with code 1 and writes a connection failure error to stderr when get_workspace raises HubConnectionError.

edge_case_tests.input: async startup helper invoked; get_workspace raises HubConnectionError
edge_case_tests.expected: process exits with code 1; stderr contains a message indicating a connection failure

edge_case_tests.description: The async startup helper treats an empty workspace.git_url as a mismatch against any non-empty local origin URL and exits with the URL mismatch error.

edge_case_tests.expected: process exits with code 1; stderr shows both URLs (empty and local) and a 'cd' instruction
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: workspace = Workspace(workspace_mode='carry_patch', clone_status='ready', git_url=''); with mock_hub_client(get_workspace_returns=workspace), mock_subprocess_run(returncode=0, stdout=b'https://git.example.com/repo.git\n'): with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); assert exc_info.value.code == 1; assert 'cd' in captured_stderr

edge_case_tests.description: nightshift writes .nightshift/config.toml successfully when .nightshift/ directory already exists but config.toml is absent.

edge_case_tests.expected: .nightshift/config.toml is created successfully with expected TOML content
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: with tmp_cwd() as cwd: (cwd / '.nightshift').mkdir(); run_config_generation(hub_url='https://hub.example.com', slug='my-slug'); assert (cwd / '.nightshift' / 'config.toml').exists()

edge_case_tests.description: nightshift emits logging.warning and continues when the atomic rename of config.toml.tmp to config.toml raises an exception.
preconditions: os.rename is mocked to raise OSError after temp file is written
edge_case_tests.input: config generation triggered; temp file write succeeds but rename raises OSError
edge_case_tests.expected: logging.warning is called; nightshift continues running; config.toml.tmp may remain on disk
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: with mock_os_rename(raises=OSError('rename failed')), capture_logs() as logs: run_config_generation_and_continue(); warning_messages = [r for r in logs if r.levelname == 'WARNING']; assert len(warning_messages) >= 1; assert startup_continued_normally()

edge_case_tests.expected: generated TOML contains 'integration_branch = "main"'
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: with tmp_cwd() as cwd: run_config_generation(integration_branch='main'); content = (cwd / '.nightshift' / 'config.toml').read_text(); assert 'integration_branch = "main"' in content

edge_case_tests.description: The global AgentFoxConfig TOML template in config_gen.py includes [hub] and [carry_patch] sections with comment annotations.

edge_case_tests.input: Read the global TOML template string from config_gen.py
edge_case_tests.expected: template string contains '[hub]' and '[carry_patch]' sections

edge_case_tests.description: When the first set_variable call raises an exception, nightshift emits logging.warning and still attempts the second set_variable call for AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH.
preconditions: set_variable is mocked to raise HubConnectionError on the first call and succeed on the second
edge_case_tests.input: async startup helper invoked; first set_variable raises HubConnectionError
edge_case_tests.expected: logging.warning is called once; set_variable is called twice (both AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC and AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH); nightshift continues
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: call_count = [0]; def side_effect(*args): call_count[0] += 1; if call_count[0] == 1: raise HubConnectionError(); with mock_hub_client(set_variable_side_effect=side_effect), capture_logs() as logs: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); assert call_count[0] == 2; assert any(r.levelname == 'WARNING' for r in logs)

edge_case_tests.description: set_variable completes without error when the variables are already set to 'false' on the hub (idempotent PATCH-then-POST upsert).
preconditions: HubClient.set_variable is mocked to succeed (simulating idempotent upsert)
edge_case_tests.input: async startup helper invoked; set_variable called when variables already set to 'false'
edge_case_tests.expected: set_variable completes without raising any exception; no warning log is emitted
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: with mock_hub_client(set_variable_returns=None), capture_logs() as logs: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); assert not any(r.levelname == 'WARNING' for r in logs if 'set_variable' in r.message.lower() or 'AUTO_REBUILD' in r.message)

edge_case_tests.description: The async startup helper executes within a single event loop created by asyncio.run() without raising RuntimeError from a pre-existing running loop.

test is run from a synchronous context (not inside an existing event loop)
edge_case_tests.input: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)) called from synchronous main()
edge_case_tests.expected: no RuntimeError is raised; the event loop is created and destroyed by asyncio.run()
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: try: asyncio.run(startup_helper(...)); except RuntimeError as e: assert False, f'RuntimeError raised: {e}'
